titre_chapitre: Make-to-Stock Production and the Kanban System

questions.enonce: What is the primary philosophy behind the make-to-start (make-to-stock) production approach?
options: Customers wait for production to start only after they place a firm order.
Customers immediately take products from an existing stock, and production is triggered backward when stock levels drop below a critical threshold.
Production is completely automated without any human intervention or inventory.
Purchasing orders are generated randomly regardless of consumer demand.
questions.explication: In make-to-stock approaches, customers buy from existing stock, and when items are taken, it triggers production at preceding workstations in a backward pull system[span_0](start_span)[span_0](end_span).

questions.enonce: What is a Kanban label used for in a production system?
options: To materialize the order placed by a customer workstation to a supplier workstation, signaling what needs to be replenished[span_1](start_span)[span_1](end_span).
To track the individual salaries of factory employees.
To calculate the retail price of the product for the market.
To determine long-term strategic investments over a 3-year horizon.
questions.explication: A Kanban label is a physical or digital ticket used to manage flow and communicate orders from a customer workstation to a supplier workstation[span_2](start_span)[span_2](end_span).

questions.enonce: How do Kanban tables help manage production and avoid constant running?
options: They use different zones (green, orange, red) to indicate stock criticality and signal when production needs to be re-launched[span_3](start_span)[span_3](end_span).
They automatically delete empty labels to reduce paperwork.
They calculate the learning curve coefficient of workers.
They set the exact profit margin for the company.
questions.explication: Kanban tables use zones like green, orange, and red to track empty labels and inform workstations when stock is reaching critical levels, indicating when to trigger production[span_4](start_span)[span_4](end_span).

questions.enonce: What is a key focus of Industry 4.0 (Industry of the Future) in modern production management?
options: Maximizing the physical use of paper documents across all workshops.
Introducing digital technologies, process optimization, and intelligent connected equipment to react more quickly to market changes[span_5](start_span)[span_5](end_span).
Eliminating all forms of automation and returning entirely to manual labor.
Restricting manufacturing to a single standard product.
questions.explication: Industry 4.0 integrates digital technologies and connected, smart equipment into production management to optimize processes and increase operational efficiency[span_6](start_span)[span_6](end_span).

questions.enonce: Besides operational time performance, what major trend is increasingly integrated into modern production management as highlighted in the conclusion?
options: Sustainable production and environmental awareness (such as working with ADEME)[span_7](start_span)[span_7](end_span)
The complete abolition of customer delivery deadlines
Focusing exclusively on financial banking cycles
Increasing fossil fuel consumption
questions.explication: Sustainable production and environmental awareness are major modern trends, notably involving collaboration and priorities set by agencies like ADEME[span_8](start_span)[span_8](end_span).
